To get $d$-dimensional theory, we sum up all possible frequencies on the circle(so called Matsubara frequency summation) which gives $d$-dimensional thermal partition function. We note that the nontrivial $t$-dependence appears beyond classical limit. To take into account quantum effects, we solve the Hamiltonian dynamics by keeping $\hbar$ corrections. The spectral deformation is mediated by a parameter $l$ such that $\mu=\beta^{-1}\log l$ and so we call this $l$-deformation. This is related to the initial boundary condition of the Schrodinger equation. We also note that the two theories are not equivalent to each other and we just check their correspondence at the level of one-loop determinant, i.e. zero point function in the note.
item.dc:creator: WooCheol Shin, Jun Hyuk Lee, Ji-seong Chae, Jae-Hyuk Oh

item.title: Fate of Bouncing Singularities at Finite $G_N$
item.description: arXiv:2609.31309v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The gravity approximation to a thermal two-point function can develop a complex-time singularity associated with a trajectory that reaches the black-hole singularity. We show that the corresponding singularity is absent at finite $G_N$. This is done by extending Conformal Field Theory analyticity properties to the second sheet (and to the universal cover). We also put two different upper bounds on the amplitude of the correlator at the would-be singularity, by certain finite partial sums, and by a certain partition function on a manifold with nontrivial topology, where two thermal geometries are glued. We discuss the possible implications for the black hole singularity.
item.dc:creator: Zohar Komargodski

item.title: Monopoles, duality, and energy splitting in Chern-Simons QED$_3$
item.description: arXiv:2609.37795v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We compute the scaling dimensions of monopole operators in QED$_3$ with $N$ 2-component complex fermions and Chern-Simons level $k$ to subleading order in the limit where $k,N$ are large and $k/N$ is fixed, which generalizes previous results for scalar QED$_3$ (sQED$_3$) coupled to $N$ complex scalars. In both cases, at leading large $N$ many monopole operators are degenerate, and we compute their energy splitting. We use these results to check the duality between QED$_3$ with $N=1,k=-3/2$ and sQED$_3$ with $N=1,k=2$, whose $U(1)$ monopole symmetry is enhanced to $SO(3)$. We find the scaling dimensions in each dual theory match to high precision for all charges, the lowest charge spin 1 monopoles are close to 2 as expected for the emergent $SO(3)$ current, and the degenerate second lowest charge monopoles match a prediction from a fuzzy sphere calculation, including the energy splitting. We also find similar evidence for dualities between QED$_3$ with $N=1,k=-(2m+1)/2$ and one scalar coupled to two $U(1)$ gauge fields, which has an effective description as sQED$_3$ with $N=1,k=\frac{m+1}{m}$ and $q_s=mq_f$ for $m>1$. Finally, we also find similar evidence for Son's duality between QED$_3$ with $N=1,k=0$ and a free fermion, and clarify a previously discussed match between sQED$_3$ with $N=k=1$ dual to a free fermion.
item.dc:creator: Shai M. Chester, \'Eric Dupuis

item.title: Random wave chaos on momentum-fractionated microstate geometries
item.description: arXiv:2610.15918v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the role of momentum fractionation in the development of chaos on smooth 3-charge supergravity solutions of D1-D5 theory, specifically momentum-fractionated superstrata. We probe the chaos through the dynamics of null geodesics and waves. On fractionated backgrounds, both geodesics and waves show uniformly strong chaos (large chaotic sea and near-perfect agreement with the Berry random wave hypothesis). In contrast, geodesics and waves on single-mode (non-fractionated) superstrata are closer to separability (although still chaotic). We discuss a possibility that such dichotomy can be related to the expectation that monotone BPS states are less chaotic than fortuitous ones. Finally, we explain why our chaos probes are meaningful for microstate geometries even though they become trivial in the black hole limit.
item.dc:creator: Vladan Djuki\'c, Mihailo \v{C}ubrovi\'c

item.title: Non-Coulomb $Q$-cohomology and quantum lifting
item.description: arXiv:2610.22332v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study quantum lifting of classical $Q$-cohomology classes in four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=4$ super-Yang--Mills theory. Certain powers of the gaugino bilinear $\mathcal{S}=\text{Tr}(\lambda_+\lambda_-)$ in orthogonal theories provide non-Coulomb monotones: multi-graviton classes that vanish upon Cartan restriction. For $SO(7)$, we identify $\mathcal S^4$ as a superconformal descendant of a known lifted monotone class, explaining the latter's non-Coulomb character. We explicitly construct a fortuitous lifting partner for $\mathcal S^4$ that is, by contrast, visible on the Coulomb branch. This construction provides a strategy for finding analogous partners for higher powers at higher ranks. Our main result establishes restrictions on quantum lifting in the multi-trace sector of the classical gauge-group families. We show that the one-loop correction $Q_1$ to the supercharge annihilates every monotone class in classical cohomology, while every $[Q_1]$ image has vanishing Cartan restriction. Thus every non-zero one-loop pairing has a fortuitous source and a non-Coulomb target, and Coulomb monotones survive at this order at finite rank. In the BMN sector, our results imply that non-Coulomb monotones also survive at one loop. A crucial step shows that dressing any classical class by a sufficiently high power of a scalar discriminant yields a multi-graviton class, or zero in cohomology when the original class is non-Coulomb. We interpret this annihilation as a partial no-hair property.
item.dc:creator: Tanay Kibe, Sam van Leuven, Kayleigh Mathieson

item.title: One-loop unifying relations between Yang-Mills theory and the nonlinear sigma model from Berends-Giele currents
item.description: arXiv:2610.25972v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study unifying relations between Yang-Mills theory and the nonlinear sigma model. We extend tree-level amplitude relations expressed through differential operators to off-shell multiparticle currents and obtain one-loop integrand relations by sewing two off-shell legs. This off-shell approach may also apply to higher-loop integrands.
item.dc:creator: Zhenhua Guo, Xin Yan

item.title: Can componentwise D7-tadpole cancellation yield a chiral Standard Model? A no-go for smooth O7$^{-}$ orientifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.28730v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a componentwise prescription for D7-tadpole cancellation that includes, as a special case, the local cancellation used in several moduli-stabilisation constructions. We first consider smooth Type IIB Calabi--Yau orientifolds with O7$^{-}$ components of pairwise distinct divisor classes. For each component class $[R_i]$, eight covering-space D7-branes are distributed among smooth irreducible representatives of that class in an orientifold-compatible way. Each component sector may therefore contain several orthogonal, unitary, or symplectic parent factors. We show that these configurations cannot supply the chiral Standard Model through their perturbative D7 spectrum. Without symplectic factors, the entire parent algebra of each component sector embeds into $\mathfrak{so}(8)$ and cannot contain commuting color and weak-isospin subalgebras. Disjointness excludes massless fermions connecting different component sectors, so quark-doublet fermions are absent. Configurations containing symplectic factors require a separate argument: massless hypercharge, together with the same disjointness, forces the net quark-doublet chirality to vanish. Both arguments allow admissible D7 gauge backgrounds and diagonal gauge embeddings, with no restriction on $h^{1,1}_{-}(X)$. We then allow repeated O7 classes, whose D7 sectors can have larger parent groups but necessarily have zero net chirality for both Abelian and non-Abelian gauge backgrounds. We also extend the obstruction to mixed allocations with Whitney remainders supporting no continuous gauge group. We give a geometric condition under which the tadpole forces purely local cancellation. For a specified finite set of allowed D7 support classes, a separate test identifies component sectors in which the tadpole forces componentwise cancellation. We discuss applications to toric constructions and axion potentials.
item.dc:creator: Mudit Jain

item.title: Spectral flow in AdS$\mathbf{_3}$ revisited
item.description: arXiv:2611.06295v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We revisit an old idea that spectral flow in WZW models can be associated with certain $G$-bundles over a worldsheet. This allows us to introduce a novel method for computing correlators of spectrally-flowed vertex operators in WZW models with group $G$ and level $k$, by systematically computing the contribution from a network of line defects. Specialising to the case of $G=SL(2, \mathbb{R})$, as is relevant to AdS$_3$ string theory, we demonstrate that generic $n$-point functions of spectrally-flowed vertex operators at tree level can be rewritten in terms of an $(n+1)$-point function of $n$ unflowed vertex operators and one degenerate insertion. This is to be interpreted as an unflowed $n$-point function in an instanton background. Moreover, we conjecture that this $(n+1)$-point function can be recast as an $n$-point function of unflowed operators and we provide evidence for this. We demonstrate that the $(n+1)$-point function satisfies the same constraints from global spacetime conformal invariance as does an unflowed $n$-point function for a specific choice of spacetime coordinates that we determine. We verify that our results agree with bootstrap results in the literature. This provides the next step towards fully solving the $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ WZW model.
item.dc:creator: Nathan McStay, Ronald Reid-Edwards, Sean Seet

item.title: Principles of Quantum Communication Theory: A Modern Approach
item.description: arXiv:2011.04672v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This is a preliminary version of a book in progress on the theory of quantum communication. We adopt an information-theoretic perspective throughout and give a comprehensive account of fundamental results in quantum communication theory from the past decade (and earlier), with an emphasis on the modern one-shot-to-asymptotic approach that underlies much of today's state-of-the-art research in this field. In Part I, we cover mathematical preliminaries and provide a detailed study of quantum mechanics from an information-theoretic perspective. We also provide an extensive and thorough review of quantum entropies, and we devote an entire chapter to the study of entanglement measures. Equipped with these essential tools, in Part II we study classical communication (with and without entanglement assistance), entanglement distillation, quantum communication, secret key distillation, and private communication. In Part III, we cover the latest developments in feedback-assisted communication tasks, such as quantum and classical feedback-assisted communication, LOCC-assisted quantum communication, and secret key agreement.
item.dc:creator: Sumeet Khatri, Ludovico Lami, Mark M. Wilde

item.title: Are magnetic fields in cosmic voids primordial?
item.description: arXiv:2505.14774v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The existence and origin of magnetic fields in cosmic voids remains an open question: Observational evidence inferred from gamma-ray spectra of TeV blazars has been debated for over a decade, while early-Universe magnetogenesis models typically invoke physics beyond the Standard Model of particle physics. We propose a late-Universe contribution to void fields from the dipole components of galactic magnetic fields. In the conducting intergalactic medium, these fields spread through turbulent magnetic diffusion, and the galaxies residing within voids reduce the required propagation distance to a few Mpc, a scale bracketed by current estimates of the turbulent diffusivity. In the regime where the propagation distance is sufficient, the superposition of randomly oriented galactic dipoles produces volume-filling void fields with a white-noise spectrum and amplitudes well above the lower bounds inferred from the absence of GeV halos around TeV blazars. These fields constitute an astrophysical background that must be accounted for before void fields are interpreted as relics of primordial magnetogenesis, and they could account for the void fields without requiring primordial fields at all. Their white-noise spectrum provides a distinctive observational signature.
item.dc:creator: Deepen Lark, Ruth Durrer, Jennifer Schober

item.title: Quintessential Inflation in Light of ACT DR6
item.description: arXiv:2511.19898v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We analyze the canonical generalized-exponential quintessential-inflation potential in light of ACT DR6 scalar-tilt constraints and the distinct demands of its post-inflationary and late-time evolution. The potential slow-roll hierarchy is derived through fourth order and checked against a numerical scalar and tensor mode calculation. For a benchmark $n=15$, $\lambda=10^{-9}$ at a reference $60$ remaining e-folds, the numerical spectrum gives $n_s\simeq0.96396$, $r\simeq7.71\times10^{-5}$, and a negative running of running of order $10^{-5}$. The exact Hubble-flow endpoint gives a full inflationary excursion exceeding $M_{\rm Pl}$ even though the ten-e-fold observable interval is much smaller. We characterize a phenomenological radiation-injection family followed through kination, radiation and matter domination, and calculate leading-order gravitational-wave transfer spectra with an integrated radiation-density test. A shallow exponential term permits a calibrated late-time quintessence phase, whose homogeneous equation of state and expansion predictions are evaluated numerically. The result is a quantitative map of the coupled inflation, reheating, gravitational-wave and dark-energy requirements, with the limitations of the assumed transfer and thermal history stated explicitly.
item.dc:creator: Sayantan Choudhury, Swapnil Kumar Singh, Satish Kumar Sahoo

item.title: Searching for Cosmological Collider in the Planck CMB Data II: collider templates and Modal analysis
item.description: arXiv:2512.22085v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Signatures of massive particles during inflation are highly informative targets for cosmological experiments. With recent progress on both theoretical and observational frontiers, we have reached the point where these novel signals of primordial non-Gaussianities (PNG) can be systematically tested with increasingly precise data. In this paper, we present the results of improved CMB data analysis for cosmological collider signals using Planck CMB data. To set the stage, we first construct a set of simplified but characteristic collider templates which are accurate over a broad range of particle masses, spins and sound speeds. In order to break degeneracies with single-field PNG, we propose an orthogonalization scheme such that the collider templates are uncorrelated with the highly constrained equilateral and orthogonal shapes. On this basis, we deploy the Modal bispectrum estimator for the Planck analysis and perform a systematic scan of parameters to search for the most significant collider signal. The maximum signal-to-noise ratio is found to be $2.35\sigma$ for an orthogonalized massive spin-0 exchange after taking into account the look-elsewhere effect. In addition, we cross-validate the Modal analysis with the CMB-BEST pipeline, which demonstrates the consistency of results across the benchmark examples of collider templates. Given the low signal-to-noise ratio regime we find at the current stage of PNG observations, we believe the orthogonalization procedure provides an optimized strategy for future tests of the cosmological collider signals.
item.dc:creator: Petar Suman, Dong-Gang Wang, Wuhyun Sohn, James R. Fergusson, E. P. S. Shellard

item.title: Detection of Gravitational Anomaly at Low Acceleration from a Highest-quality Sample of 36 Wide Binaries with Accurate 3D Velocities
item.description: arXiv:2601.21728v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We set out to accurately measure gravity in the low-acceleration range $(10^{-11},10^{-9})\,{\rm m}\,{\rm s}^{-2}$ from 3D motions of isolated wide binary stars. Gaia DR3 provides precise measurements of the four sky-plane components of the 3D relative displacement and velocity ($\mathbf{r}, \mathbf{v}$) for a system, but not comparably precise line-of-sight (radial) separation and velocity $v_{r}$. Based on our new observations and the public databases/publications, we assemble a sample of 36 nearby (distance $<150$pc) wide binaries in the low-acceleration regime with relatively accurate values of $v_r$. Kinematic contaminants such as undetected stellar companions are well under control using various observational diagnostics such as Gaia's {\tt ruwe} parameter, the color-magnitude diagram, multi-epoch observations of radial velocities, Speckle interferometric follow-up observations, and requiring Hipparcos-Gaia proper motion consistency. For $\Gamma \equiv \log_{10}\sqrt{\gamma}$ with $\gamma \equiv G/G_{\rm N}$ (where $G$ is a parameter generalizing Newton's constant $G_{\rm N}$), we find $\Gamma=0.102_{-0.021}^{+0.028}$ for $<10^{-9.1}\,{\rm m}\,{\rm s}^{-2}$ ($0.132_{-0.027}^{+0.035}$ for $<10^{-9.5}\,{\rm m}\,{\rm s}^{-2}$) giving a gravity boost factor of $\gamma=1.60_{-0.14}^{+0.24}$, which rules out Newton. This strong anomaly is dominated by two systems (the pairs of HD 189739, HD 189760, and TYC 259-236-1, TYC 259-906-1) that have 3D relative velocities exceeding their estimated Newtonian escape velocities. Without them, we have $\Gamma=0.042_{-0.024}^{+0.027}$ for $<10^{-9.1}\,{\rm m}\,{\rm s}^{-2}$, $0.057_{-0.031}^{+0.035}$ for $<10^{-9.5}\,{\rm m}\,{\rm s}^{-2}$, and $0.085_{-0.045}^{+0.059}$ for $<10^{-10.1}\,{\rm m}\,{\rm s}^{-2}$. Future radial velocity monitoring and Speckle interferometric imaging for larger samples will be useful to refine the present result.
item.dc:creator: K. -H. Chae, B. -C. Lee, X. Hernandez, V. G. Orlov, D. Lim, D. A. Turnshek, Y. -W. Lee

item.title: Mixed Freeze-In and Freeze-Out Histories and Dark-Sector Decays in a $\mathbb{Z}_4$ Two-Scalar Model
item.description: arXiv:2602.18564v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study dark matter production in a renormalisable $\mathbb{Z}_4$ Higgs-portal model containing a complex scalar $S_A$ and a real scalar $S_B$, where one or both states remain out of thermal equilibrium with the Standard Model bath. We follow their coupled evolution through conversion, semi-annihilation, and the decay $S_B\to S_A S_A$ when kinematically allowed. We impose theoretical consistency conditions, limits on invisible Higgs decays, and LZ direct-detection bounds, accounting for each component's relic fraction. We check WIMP/FIMP assignments against interaction rates. When both states are stable, we find viable FIMP--FIMP and mixed WIMP--FIMP scenarios. In mixed cases, the WIMP-like state remains constrained by its Higgs-portal interactions, with the surviving points mainly concentrated near the Higgs resonance. The FIMP-like state can, however, provide a substantial fraction of the relic density with a negligible direct-detection signal. For $M_{S_B}>2M_{S_A}$, the decay of the heavier scalar leads to three production histories: SuperWIMP production, injection-assisted freeze-out, and sequential freeze-in. The mechanism depends on parent and daughter production. These decays can increase the abundance of a WIMP after freeze-out or contribute to the final abundance of a FIMP, changing the relation between the daughter's Higgs coupling and its relic density. Since the primary decays produce no Standard Model particles, electromagnetic and hadronic BBN bounds on visible decay products do not apply directly. We find $r_{\rm BBN}\ll1$ throughout the retained sample. To assess effects on structure formation, we use the dark matter fraction produced through decays and an equivalent thermal-WDM mass as approximate diagnostics. Some late-decay configurations are flagged as potentially warm, whereas the sequential freeze-in sample satisfies $m_{\rm WDM}^{\rm eq}\gtrsim1~\mathrm{MeV}$.
item.dc:creator: J. P. Carvalho-Corr\^ea, B. A. Couto e Silva, B. L. S\'anchez-Vega

item.title: Chiral vortical effect and boundary-induced vortical pumping in finite Weyl systems
item.description: arXiv:2604.01293v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The chiral vortical effect (CVE) -- an axial current driven by rotation in chiral matter -- appears in systems ranging from relativistic fluids to Weyl semimetals. We present a quantum treatment of a rotating Weyl fermion in a finite cylinder that reproduces the on-axis current density obtained by Vilenkin in an infinite system, while revealing two new phenomena. First, we find that the cross-sectional averaged current density vanishes in the thermodynamic limit, establishing that the bulk vortical response is purely a magnetization current. Second, for spin-polarized boundary conditions, we uncover a robust family of chiral modes that transport axial charge, $\Delta Q=\chi N^2\Delta\theta/4\pi$, under rotation by angle $\Delta\theta$, where $\chi$ is the Weyl node chirality and $N$ is the number of chiral modes. The pump is independent of temperature, Fermi level, and Weyl velocities, but depends on the UV-sensitive number $N$. These results clarify the quantum structure of the bulk CVE and reveal a boundary-enforced chiral spectral structure underlying vortical response in Weyl systems.
item.dc:creator: B. Q. Song, Pavan Hosur

item.title: Planckian dissipation from classical hydrodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2605.19450v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Hydrodynamics describes the long-time, long-distance dynamics of interacting quantum systems by classical equations, yet at low temperature quantum fluctuations might eventually invalidate this classical picture. Here we ask what it takes for a quantum system to sustain a consistently classical hydrodynamic description. Our starting point is the quantum fluctuation-dissipation theorem which, when read in the time domain, acts as a blurring of the fine details of correlation functions on a Planckian time-scale. We analyse how this blurring interacts with the diffusive large-deviation form of correlators assuming the existence of a hydrodynamic light cone velocity, and show that the interior of the cone splits into a classical region, where correlation and response satisfy the classical fluctuation-dissipation relation, and a quantum region, where they deviate sharply from it. We illustrate the mechanism on three phenomenological hydrodynamic equations - diffusion, telegraph and diffusive-telegraph. Preserving a finite classical region as the temperature is lowered forces the current relaxation rate to be bounded from above by the Planckian rate. This bound connects to bounds on diffusivity, equilibration time and shear viscosity. In this way, a Planckian bound on dissipation emerges not as a quantum constraint on microscopic dynamics, but as the price a system pays to remain describable by classical hydrodynamics down to low temperatures.
item.dc:creator: Laura Foini, Jorge Kurchan, Silvia Pappalardi

item.title: Static Quark-Antiquark Interactions in Rotating SU(3) Gluodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2607.26939v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study static quark--antiquark interactions in rotating SU(3) gluodynamics using quenched lattice simulations at imaginary angular velocity. At zero temperature, we extract the static potential from Wilson loops for quark--antiquark pairs aligned with the rotation axis, for transverse pairs with one source on the rotation axis, and for symmetric transverse pairs across the rotation axis. Within the present accuracy, no significant rotation dependence or anisotropy is observed in the zero-temperature potential. At finite temperature, imaginary rotation suppresses the color-averaged free energies obtained from Polyakov-loop correlators in both longitudinal and transverse geometries. Axial-diagonal comparisons are used to identify a bulk region where open-boundary artifacts are reduced. In this region, the large-distance longitudinal free-energy shift is well described by $\Delta F_z(R_{xy})=A R_{xy}^2+B$. The transverse channels exhibit the same qualitative suppression, while their distance dependence additionally reflects the radial arrangement of the static sources and is compatible with a radial single-source free-energy shift in the bulk region. For the finite-temperature observables studied above $T_c$, the response weakens as the temperature is increased. These results provide lattice evidence for a position- and geometry-dependent response of bare static-source free energies to imaginary rotation in a gluonic medium.
item.dc:creator: Heng-Tong Ding, Olaf Kaczmarek, Ran Luo, Hai-Tao Shu

item.title: Massive quantum divergence on the Cauchy horizon of a black hole
item.description: arXiv:2609.10755v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate a quantum {\it massive} scalar field in the interior of a charged and spherically-symmetric (Reissner-Nordstr\"om) black hole. We examine the behaviour for varying values of the black hole charge, field mass and coupling constant when the field is in two quantum states: Hartle-Hawking (representing a black hole in thermal equilibrium) and Unruh (representing a black hole evaporating via the emission of Hawking radiation). We show that the vacuum polarization (in both states) generically {\it diverges} on the Cauchy horizon, in stark contrast to what happens for massless fields; also, the angular components of the quantum stress-energy tensor generically {\it diverge} on the Cauchy horizon and, in at least one of the two states, they do so more strongly than for massless fields. Furthermore, we calculate the energy fluxes in Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates $\{u,v\}$. We show that these fluxes in both states on the Cauchy horizon do not generically vanish. This implies, in particular, that in regular, Kruskal coordinates $\{U,V\}$ the ingoing flux diverges like $V^{-2}$ on the Cauchy horizon (where $V=0$). This divergence suggests that its backreaction via the semiclassical Einstein equations would yield a strong singularity, as opposed to its weaker, classical counterpart. Interestingly, there are exceptions, in which the energy fluxes in Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates vanish: (i) in the extremal limit (where the black hole is maximally charged); (ii) certain fine-tuned regions of parameter space, where the fluxes change sign.

item.title: On Algebraic Background-Independence
item.description: arXiv:2610.22042v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: It has recently been claimed that algebraic methods can be used to give a background-independent description of semiclassical gravity. This paper aims to provide an entry point into recent algebraic approaches to quantum gravity and to analyse and critically assess the conception of background-independence here involved. We discuss an algebraic framework for formulating an algebra of observables along the worldline of an observer in a cosmological setting. By 'gravitationally dressing' the observables to the observer's worldline, the reference to the spacetime background can be set aside at the level of the abstract *-algebra. Thus this *-algebra is taken to be independent of any particular spacetime realisation, with different states on the algebra corresponding to different backgrounds. We compare this algebraic framework to three influential notions of background-independence in the literature and argue that none of these fully captures the sense in which the *-algebra is taken to be background-independent. Building on this, we extract a novel notion of algebraic background-independence tied to the representation-independence of the *-algebra. This algebraic conception motivates two further concepts of background-independence tailored to semiclassical theories: semiclassical background-independence and perturbative background-independence. We suggest that these provide useful tools for evaluating the scope and limitations of semiclassical approaches to quantum gravity.

item.title: Minimal-length kinematics of coherent light and a proposed two-color vacuum chronoscopy
item.description: arXiv:2610.26892v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The unification of quantum theory and general relativity suggests the existence of a minimal measurable length, leading to a generalized uncertainty principle (GUP) and an energy-dependent vacuum group velocity. Testing these effects with macroscopic objects typically encounters the ``soccer-ball problem,'' where applying Planck-scale deformations to the total momentum predicts observationally ruled-out velocity deviations. We adopt the prescription, natural in quantum field theory (QFT), in which the GUP modifies single-mode commutators, and verify by explicit calculation that the macroscopic group velocity of a multimode coherent pulse reduces to the single-photon GUP velocity evaluated at the central wavelength, multiplied by the classical Gaussian-beam factor, with no dependence on the total pulse energy. The energy--momentum relation $E=pc$ itself is unmodified; the deformation enters through the velocity--momentum relation and is equivalent to a modified dispersion relation in the wave vector, with a quadratic coefficient that depends on which of the two variables is used. The soccer-ball problem --- which arises only when the GUP is applied to the center-of-mass momentum of a composite system --- is therefore absent for coherent light, and macroscopic petawatt pulses probe the same parameter space as single high-energy photons. Building on this framework, we propose a two-color vacuum chronoscopy experiment using a short-pulse petawatt laser and its high-harmonic generation. By systematically varying the macroscopic beam waist, our setup separates Planck-scale kinematic shifts from classical diffraction delays, establishing a controlled, source-independent terrestrial methodology whose sensitivity we assess against current astrophysical bounds and against the dominant waist-independent systematics that limit it, residual-gas dispersion and the harmonic birth-time offset.
